# @rxova/react-inputs

> The whole Rxova input suite from one install: locale-aware currency, fractional
> ratings, and one-time codes. Headless, accessible, zero runtime dependencies,
> no stylesheet to import. `sideEffects: false`, so your bundler drops whatever
> you do not import — this package and the individual ones are equivalent.

## Install

    npm install @rxova/react-inputs

`react >= 18` and `react-dom >= 18` are the peer dependencies.

## Minimal working example

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { CurrencyInput, Rating, OtpInput } from '@rxova/react-inputs'

export function Checkout() {
  const [price, setPrice] = useState<number | null>(null)
  const [score, setScore] = useState(0)
  const [code, setCode] = useState('')

  return (
    <>
      <CurrencyInput locale="en-US" currency="USD" value={price} onValueChange={setPrice} />
      <Rating value={score} onChange={setScore} precision={0.5} label="Rate your meal" />
      <OtpInput length={6} value={code} onChange={setCode} label="One-time code" />
    </>
  )
}
```

## What it re-exports

This package adds no API of its own. It re-exports each component package
verbatim, so the props, the CSS custom properties and the `data-*` attributes are
documented with the package that owns them — and each of those packages ships its
own `llms.txt` with a full prop table.

| Component | Package | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CurrencyInput`, `useCurrencyInput`, `currencyForCountry` | `@rxova/react-intl-currency-input` | Money entry that is correct in every locale, with no caret jumps. |
| `Rating`, `useRating` | `@rxova/react-rating-input` | Any icon, any precision. A real `radiogroup` when interactive. |
| `OtpInput`, `OtpGroup`, `OtpSlot`, `OtpSeparator`, `useOtpInput`, `useWebOTP` | `@rxova/react-otp-input` | One-time codes over one real `<input>`, with paste and SMS autofill intact. |

Every type is re-exported too — `CurrencyInputProps`, `RatingProps`,
`OtpInputProps` and the rest.

## Three mistakes to avoid

1. **Installing the individual packages to "keep the bundle small".** It makes no
   difference: `sideEffects: false` means an unused component never reaches your
   bundle either way. Install whichever suits the project; they are equivalent.
2. **Importing a stylesheet.** There is none in any of these packages. Everything
   visual is a CSS custom property or a `data-*` hook.
3. **Assuming the three components share a value convention.** They do not, on
   purpose, because their values are different things: `CurrencyInput` emits
   `number | null` via `onValueChange`, `Rating` emits `number` via `onChange`,
   and `OtpInput` emits `string` via `onChange`. Check the component's own
   `llms.txt` before wiring a form.
